articles.title: Quoting Terk Terkowitz
articles.summary: If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for. — Terk Terkowitz, An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI Tags: amazon, generative-ai, agentic-engineering, ai, llms

articles.title: You can just ask AI to do things
articles.summary: One of the most important skills in working with AI is agency: being willing to try new and ambitious things. This is true for what you build, but it’s also true for how you build. AI models are improving so quickly that most of us are bottlenecked1 on noticing that AI agents can help automate particular tasks. Here are some examples of that from my daily work. articles.title: Getting good at AI takes time and practice
articles.summary: Many people think1 that getting “good at AI” is trivial. Sure, with some early models there were tricks you had to learn,2 but current models don’t need them. Even if there are different tricks3 that work on current models, the next generation will render them obsolete, so why bother? Just tell the model what you want it to do. articles.title: Elegance and intelligence are anticorrelated
articles.summary: Elegance and intelligence can have a surprisingly negative correlation. Intelligent people sometimes produce inelegant solutions because they’re capable of rapidly brute-forcing problems.
